messages.content:
Assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category. Here are worked examples, then the case to code.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: I21

Example 3
Hospital course: A 34-year-old woman presented with fever, rigors, dysuria and right flank tenderness. Urine microscopy showed pyuria and culture grew Escherichia coli. Computed tomography showed a swollen right kidney with no abscess. She improved on intravenous ceftriaxone.
Answer: N10

Example 4
Hospital course: An 81-year-old woman was brought in after a fall at home. She could not weight-bear and the right leg was shortened and externally rotated. A pelvic radiograph showed a displaced subcapital fracture of the right femoral neck. She underwent hemiarthroplasty on day one.
Answer: S72

Example 5
Hospital course: A 19-year-old man presented with 18 hours of periumbilical pain that migrated to the right iliac fossa, with anorexia and a low-grade fever. There was guarding at McBurney's point and the white cell count was 15.2. Laparoscopy confirmed an inflamed, non-perforated appendix.
Answer: K35

Example 6
Hospital course: A 64-year-old woman with a history of oestrogen-receptor-positive breast carcinoma treated five years earlier presented with progressive thoracic back pain. Magnetic resonance imaging showed deposits in T7 and T9 with no cord compression. Biopsy confirmed deposits of breast origin and she received palliative radiotherapy to the spine.
Answer: C79

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Date of Admission: [INSERT DATE]
Date of Discharge: [INSERT DATE]

Patient Name: [INSERT NAME]                    MR#[INSERT MR NUMBER]
Clinical Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Medical History:
The patient had chronic renal failure, hypertension, and a history of smoking and morbid obesity.

Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted to the emergency department with exertional dyspnea, shortness of breath, and recurrent episodes of acute pulmonary edema. Upon physical examination, he had bilateral pulmonary rales, lower extremities edema, and a large pulsative mass that was noticed during abdominal examination. Emergency CT scans revealed an infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) of 9.8 cm size with communication between the aorta and the IVC without any signs of a retroperitoneal rupture. 

Treatment:
The patient underwent an emergency laparotomy and aortic cross-clamping, during which a 20 × 15 mm aortocaval communication was discovered after opening the aortic sac. The bleeding from the IVC was controlled by digital compression, and the fistula was oversawn from within the sac with monofilament sutures. After that, a 20mm Dacron tube graft was placed to restore perfusion.

Post-Surgical Management:
The patient was shifted to the ICU after surgery and received continuous venovenous haemofiltration due to acute renal failure, which resolved on the fourth postoperative day. The patient was extubated on the tenth postoperative day and discharged after 25 days of hospitalization. At discharge, he exhibited bilateral peripheral edema but no evidence of deep vein thrombosis. His edemas' have resolved, and the patient remains in good health 16 months after the operation.

Follow-up Care:
The patient's follow-up appointments for the surgical site have been scheduled. The clinical team will monitor and manage related medical symptoms and tackle his pre-existing conditions appropriately.

Answer with the three-character category only.

text:
The principal diagnosis is an infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm with an aortocaval fistula, with no signs of retroperitoneal rupture.

In ICD-10-AM, an abdominal aortic aneurysm without rupture is coded I71.4. An aneurysm with rupture is I71.3. An aortocaval fistula is an arteriovenous fistula, which could be coded I77.0 (acquired arteriovenous fistula) or Q27.3 (congenital). Here the fistula is a complication of the aneurysm, and the aneurysm is the underlying condition that drove the admission and surgery, so I71 is the best fit.

The fistula was not described as a rupture into the retroperitoneum, but the aneurysm communicated with the IVC, which is a form of contained rupture into a vein. Even so, the category stays I71 whether the aneurysm is ruptured or not.

**I71**
